# 1 Epidemiological highlights

• Epidemiological situation: A new health zone affected in Haut-Uélé province: Rungu health zone.
The cumulative total rises to 48 affected health zones out of 140 in the five provinces, of which 47 remain under active transmission.

• Coordination: Official visit of Her Excellency the Prime Minister to Tshopo and Ituri provinces to strengthen MVE-B (Ebola virus disease) response activities; Installation and launch of diagnostic laboratory activities in Kasenyi in the Tchomia health zone in Ituri.

• Case evolution: Over the past 24 hours, 68 new confirmed cases, 40 confirmed deaths and 21 recoveries were recorded:

o Ituri: 51 new confirmed cases were notified, mainly in Bunia (17), Rwampara (9), Nizi (8), Mangala (6), Komanda (3), Lita (2), Mongbwalu (2), Damas (1), Logo (1), Rimba (1) and Tchomia (1), 30 deaths among which, 60% community.

o Nord-Kivu: 15 new confirmed cases were reported (Katwa 12, Butembo 1, Musienene 1, and Beni 1) as well as 10 deaths, including 80% community and 2 in CTEs (Ebola treatment centre).
The provincial cumulative total reaches 290 confirmed cases and 182 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 62,8%.

o Haut-Uélé: 2 new confirmed cases (1 case in Rungu and 1 case in Wamba) and 0 deaths were reported.
A new health zone is affected, namely: Rungu health zone.
The provincial cumulative total rises to 29 confirmed cases and 15 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 51,7 %, distributed across 5 health zones out of 13 in the province.

o Sud-Kivu and Tshopo: No new confirmed cases or deaths were reported.
Cumulative totals remain at 5 cases, 4 deaths and 1 recovered in Tshopo and 3 cases including 1 death in Sud-Kivu, where Miti-Murhesa health zone totals 56 days without a new confirmed case.

• Analysis: Ituri remains the epicentre of the outbreak, concentrating 89,0 % of cumulative cases and 75,0 % of the day's new confirmations.
Contact tracing performance remains insufficient and requires a strengthening of surveillance activities.

EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT

Declared on 15 May 2026, the 17th Ebola virus disease (MVE) outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus continues its progression in a complex humanitarian and security context.
Initially confined to the Mongbwalu health zone (Ituri), it has spread to five provinces (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo), now affecting 48 health zones.
Population movements, insecurity, artisanal mining activities and cross-border trade with Uganda and South Sudan continue to promote transmission.
Multisectoral coordination remains mobilised to strengthen surveillance, intensify response interventions and limit the spread of the outbreak.

## 2.3 Mapping of confirmed cases

The spatial distribution confirms transmission mainly concentrated in Ituri, particularly in the health zones of Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Nizi, Nyankunde and Lita, with continued transmission in already affected zones and an extension towards the new health zone of Rungu in Haut-Uélé.

[FIGURE: SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF HEALTH ZONES HAVING REPORTED CONFIRMED CASES]

The recent appearance of the new health zone of Rungu in Haut-Uélé confirms a progressive extension of affected zones, highlighting the need to simultaneously maintain intensive interventions at the epicentre and preparedness activities in neighbouring provinces.

## 2.4 Temporal analysis — epidemic curves

The epidemic curve shows sustained transmission during weeks W25 to W30, with fluctuations linked to notification delays and the progressive consolidation of data.

[FIGURE: EPIDEMIC CURVE BY WEEK OF NOTIFICATION]

[FIGURE: EPIDEMIC CURVE BY DATE OF ONSET OF SYMPTOMS (DHIS2 LINE LIST)]

The epidemic remains in a phase of sustained transmission, with a high level of virus circulation.
Recent fluctuations must be interpreted with caution due to notification delays and progressive consolidation of data.

## 2.5 Demographic characteristics

The age pyramid shows a predominance of working-age adults (18–50 years).
Minors under 18 years of age and elderly people over 50 years of age are proportionally less affected.

[FIGURE: CONFIRMED CASES BY SEX AND AGE GROUP]

[FIGURE: DEATHS BY SEX AND AGE GROUP (AMONG CONFIRMED CASES)]

The distribution of cases by sex remains balanced.
The predominance of cases among working-age adults reflects more frequent community and occupational exposures, while the proportion of paediatric cases demonstrates the persistence of intrafamilial transmission.

This improvement reflects the reduction in investigation carryovers and the consolidation of data from affected provinces.
The improvement in the investigation rate is linked to the reduction in investigation carryovers and the strengthening of surveillance teams in affected provinces.

## 3.2 Laboratory: testing and positivity

→ Ituri: 155 samples documented in the collection network, of which 51 positive (33 alive and 18 deaths), representing an apparent positivity of 32,9 %.

→ Nord-Kivu: 120 samples received and analysed, among which 15 positive (7 alive and 8 deaths), representing a positivity of 12,5%.

→ Tshopo: 3 samples received and analysed.
All these samples came back negative after analysis.

• Installation and launch of diagnostic laboratory activities in Kasenyi in the Tchomia health zone in Ituri as part of DRC-Uganda cross-border coordination with the support of WHO and US CDC.
Provision of 2 RadiOne machines by WHO to the Kasenyi laboratory.

## 3.4 Points of entry and control points (PoE/PoC)

### 3.4.1 — Alerts at crossing points (24 h)

Ituri — 5 alerts notified
Five (5) alerts were notified at PoE/PoC in Ituri, All these 5 live alerts were validated and all referred to CTE/CT (transit centre).

Nord-Kivu — 5 alerts notified

It should be noted that 2 415 travellers passed through the PoE/PoC, among whom, 2 405 screened, 2 379 having washed hands and 2 415 sensitised as of the date of 22 July 2026.

# 7 Response activities by pillar

COORDINATION
Arrival of H.E. the Prime Minister in the provinces of Tshopo and Ituri; High-level strategic meeting with H.E. the Prime Minister; Provision of 10 vehicles to Ituri province; Visit to the provincial laboratory of Tshopo by H.E. the Prime Minister and the site planned for the construction of the CTE/EOC by the Governor of Tshopo; Continuation of coordination meetings and supervision of field activities; coordination of pillars and support for the installation of local laboratories.

PCI (infection prevention and control) / WASH
→ Ituri: 18 rings opened, 35 ESS monitored, 10 assessments, 9 ESS and 8 means of transport decontaminated, 182 PPL trained, 44/107 households decontaminated within 48 h.

→ Nord-Kivu: Decontamination of 4 case stay ESS including 1 in Beni, 2 in Butembo and 1 in Katwa; Provision of incomplete PCI kit in 1 ESS in Butembo (CH MALENDE); PCI scorecard assessment in 8 ESS including 1 in Beni, 5 in Butembo, and 2 in Katwa; Monitoring and support of 59 ESS including: 18 in Beni, 11 in Butembo, 2 in Katwa, 2 in Kyondo and 26 in Oïcha; Briefing of 209 ESS providers during supportive supervision visits including: 67 in Beni, 38 in Butembo, 9 in Katwa, 9 in Kyondo and 86 in Oïcha; Community deaths having received an SDB: 8 including 6 in Beni, 1 in Butembo and 1 in Oïcha; Community deaths having been subject to SWAB: 11 including 6 in Beni, 1 in Butembo, 2 in Kondo, 1 in Mabalako and 1 in Oïcha .

→ Tshopo: PCI Scorecard assessments carried out at CS Kwetu (16,1%) and CS Jamaa (37,1%).
Decontamination of 10 households (AS (health area) St André) and 2 ESS (AS St André & AS Libota).
Installation of triage service at HGR Tshopo.

SAFE AND DIGNIFIED BURIALS (EDS)
→ Ituri: 89 death alerts, 71 EDS performed, 49 swabs; EDS proportion 80 %.
Community resistance in Nyankunde and Nizi; EDS training in Tchomia.

→ Nord-Kivu: 38 Swabs performed out of 40 death alerts and 40 EDS performed.

→ Tshopo: continuation of Coordination required for community death management and safe transport of bodies.

CONTINUITY OF ESSENTIAL HEALTH SERVICES (CSSE)
→ Ituri: Continuation of health zone supervision.

COMMUNICATION (RCCE / CREC)
→ Ituri: 1.053 people were reached by awareness messages delivered by the RECO (community health worker) 54 in households of 1 out of 4 Health Zones , communities are beginning to apply hand washing without problem; 70 people were reached on awareness themes during educational talks held by community actors in health zone; 62 people including village chiefs and leaders of women's associations were engaged in response actions following community dialogue sessions conducted in the ZS (health zone);

HOLISTIC CARE (PECH)
→ Ituri: 20 new recoveries, 570 patients in isolation, 23 deaths among discharges; 1024 hot meals were served to patients including 121 to suspects, 122 to Confirmed, 723 to PPL and 58 to accompanying persons.

→ Nord-Kivu: continued monitoring of clinical management in CTE/CT.

→ Tshopo: 0 new admissions today.
4 suspected cases currently hospitalised at CTE HC Kisangani.
Performance of 2nd PCR in 2 suspects (results pending).
1 operational ambulance based at HGR Makiso.

2.755 people were reached during mass awareness sessions held by community actors in Health Zone.
(ZS AUNGBA, BUNIA, MONGBWALU): including 38 women on MVE with financial support from MEDAIR; 34 religious leaders briefed including 14 women on prevention of BUNDIBUGYO MVE in their respective settings, procedures to follow across different pillars; Training of 35 RECO, Block chiefs/Religious leaders and associations from the ISP site on MVE, Community-based surveillance, community dialogue, contact tracing at the site including 14 women with support from CARITAS (RWAMPARA, NIZI).

→ Nord-Kivu: Briefing of 38 RECO, Cell chiefs and neighbourhood chiefs on operationalisation of SBC activities, in AS KYAGHALA in the ZS of Katwa; Mass communication for 123 people on importance of contact tracing and the role of food kits distributed thanks to support from WFP.

→ Tshopo: 60 home visits carried out (360 people sensitised).
Mass awareness of 15 868 people in 5 ZS.
Training of 35 CREC members, 22 journalists, 712 RECO, 217 community leaders and 414 motorcycle taxi drivers

RESEARCH, INNOVATION & VACCINATION

# 8 Main challenges, impacts and required actions


| N° | Challenges | Impact | Required actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance towards post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at Muchanga bridge, paralysis of activities in Nyankunde) | Confirmation delay, underestimation of cases, disruption of key activities | Intensify CREC, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, increase the number of EDS teams |
| 2 | Non-payment of providers (strike in Bunia and Rwampara ZS; resumption announced following intervention by the military governor of Ituri) | Interruption of response activities, including safe and dignified burials | Regularise payment of providers; secure dedicated funding |
| 3 | Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: occupancy of 136,2 % in Nord-Kivu (bed capacity: 141) and 80,4 % in Ituri (570 patients for 709 beds); | Admission delays, increased risk of nosocomial transmission | Accelerate construction and expansion of CTEs, deploy temporary structures, systematically report bed capacities |
| 4 | Low contact tracing performance in Ituri 72,1 %; Nord-Kivu 78,9% | Unbroken chains of transmission | Train, deploy and motivate community health workers (RECO); reinforced supervision; investigate the decline observed in Ituri |
| 5 | Shortage of ambulances and prepositioning at PoC | Delays in transfer and isolation | Preposition ambulances (including at PoE/PoC), deploy CTs by ZS |
| 6 | Insufficient supply of essential generic medicines and medical consumables | Weakening of overall clinical management | Advocacy and urgent supply of essential medicines |
| 7 | Shortage of IPC supplies (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175/1 170, or 15 %) | High risk of nosocomial infections (123 PPL cases including 36 deaths) | Urgent supply, strengthening of IPC training |
| 8 | Geographical expansion (Haut-Uélé, Tshopo) and high mobility | Risk of urban, riverine and cross-border spread | Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC of Haut-Uélé; strengthen cross-border coordination |
| 9 | Installation of local laboratories (Butembo, Mambasa and Logo) | Long confirmation times, undetected transmission | Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacities |
| 10 | Insufficient financial resources | Limitation of pillar implementation | Urgent resource mobilisation, advocacy with partners |
| 11 | Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) | Restriction of operations | Strengthening of security coordination and humanitarian access |
| 12 | Continuity of essential health services (CEHS) compromised | Increase in indirect mortality (non-Ebola) | Effective implementation of free healthcare, strengthening CEHS |
